blocks.text: A relation is in BCNF when for every non-trivial FD X → A, X is a superkey. That is the whole definition — one sentence, no exceptions to memorise.

blocks.text: Every BCNF relation is in 3NF, but a 3NF relation need not be in BCNF — 3NF relaxes the superkey requirement when the right-hand side is a prime attribute.

blocks.text: BCNF's slogan: *every determinant is a key*. If some attribute or attribute group determines something without being a superkey, the relation has a second source of truth hiding inside it — updates can disagree.

R(A, B, C) with F = {AB → C, A → B}: keys = {A} (because A → B and AB → C give C). Both FDs have superkey left sides → **BCNF**. Compare with F = {AB → C, C → B}: C is not a superkey, but B is prime → only 3NF.
